transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t seem to keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I’ll start talking about my overnight shift, and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts, and people just look lost. I can tell I’m not making sense, and it’s been getting hard.
Can you describe what goes through your mind when your words start jumping around like that—does it feel like your thoughts are racing, or maybe you lose track of what you were saying?

It’s more like I lose the line of what I was saying. I’ll start with one thing, like something from my overnight shift, and then my mind grabs onto something else—soccer, or paint colors, or charts—and I’m talking about that before I even realize I switched. Then I look at people and they seem confused, and I know I didn’t get from one point to the next right.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or broadcasted so others can hear them?

I don’t think so. I mean, my thoughts feel messy and hard to follow, but I haven’t noticed them being put in my head or taken out. And I don’t feel like other people can hear them, at least not like that.
Have you been experiencing any strange or unusual perceptions, like hearing voices that others don’t hear, or seeing things that others can’t see?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been seeing things that aren’t there. And with hearing voices… I haven’t really noticed anything like a voice talking to me when no one’s around. It’s more just confusing in my own head, but not like I’m hearing someone else.
Have you had any experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to understand or agree with, even though it turned out not to be true?

Yeah… at work, I’m pretty sure the supervisors changed my shifts on purpose. Like, it’s not just random staffing. I think they’re watching me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong.

People keep telling me it’s just staffing shortages, but it doesn’t feel like that to me. It feels directed at me.
Do you believe that the supervisors are watching you through the cameras because they are trying to harm you or catch you doing something wrong?

Yeah… I think they’re trying to catch me doing something wrong, or prove I’m unsafe. I don’t know if I’d say harm me exactly, but it feels like they changed my shifts on purpose and they’re watching me on the cameras, even though people keep saying it’s just staffing.
Do you feel completely certain that your supervisors are watching you through the cameras, or do you have any doubts about it?

I feel pretty certain, honestly. I know other people say it’s just staffing shortages, but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like they changed my shifts on purpose and they’re watching me on the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong.
Has anyone been able to convince you, even a little bit, that the supervisors might not be watching you through the cameras, or does it still feel completely true to you no matter what others say?

No… not really. People have tried to tell me it’s just staffing shortages, but I don’t buy that. It still feels true to me that they changed my shifts on purpose and they’re watching me on the cameras to see if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong.
Can you think of any evidence, even small, that would suggest the supervisors aren’t watching you on the cameras or that your shifts weren’t changed on purpose?

Not really. I mean, people keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, but that doesn’t feel like evidence to me. The way my shifts changed and knowing the cameras are there… it feels like they’re watching me to see if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong. I can’t think of anything that really proves they’re not.

Have these beliefs about your supervisors watching you ever made you feel upset, anxious, or depressed, or do they just feel like something you know is true without causing you much emotional reaction?

Yeah, it definitely makes me anxious and upset. It’s not just some neutral thing in my head. When I’m at work and I see the cameras, I start thinking they’re watching me, checking if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong. It makes me feel tense, and honestly kind of depressed too, like I’m being singled out.
Has there ever been a time when you doubted, even a little, that your supervisors were watching you through the cameras, or has the idea always felt completely true to you?

I don’t really remember a time I doubted it much. Maybe for a second when someone says it’s just staffing issues, I try to consider that… but it doesn’t stick. It still feels true to me that they changed my shifts on purpose and that they’re watching me through the cameras to see if I’m unsafe or messing up.
Has there ever been a moment, even a brief one, when you felt unsure or doubted that your supervisors were watching you through the cameras?

Not really, no. I mean, maybe for a moment when someone tells me it’s just staffing shortages, I try to think about that, but it doesn’t feel right. I’m still pretty sure they changed my shifts on purpose and that they’re watching me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe.
Have you ever felt that this belief about being watched could be wrong, even for a moment, or has it always felt completely true to you no matter what?

It’s always felt true to me. I can hear what people say about staffing shortages and all that, but I don’t really believe that’s the reason. I’m sure they changed my shifts and they watch me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong.
Has there ever been any point, even the tiniest moment, where you questioned whether your belief that the supervisors are watching you could be mistaken?

No… I don’t think I’ve really questioned it. People keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, but that doesn’t make sense to me. I’m sure they changed my shifts, and they’re watching me on the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe or doing something wrong.
Has your belief that the supervisors are watching you ever felt completely certain to you, without any room for doubt at all, even when others have tried to reassure you otherwise?

Yes. It feels completely certain to me. Even when people try to say it’s just staffing shortages, I don’t buy that. I’m sure my supervisors changed my shifts on purpose, and they’re watching me through the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe.

Have your beliefs about being watched ever felt connected to how you’ve been feeling emotionally, like they make sense based on your mood, or have they felt separate from how you’ve been feeling inside?

It feels connected to how low I am. When the depression gets really bad, that’s when I’m most sure they’re watching me through the cameras. And then when I try to explain it, my words get all mixed up, like I can’t say it clearly even though it feels obvious to me.
